# Synthetic compatibility fixtures

Generated by `tools/oracle.cc`, linked against unmodified Mozc at
`c4b2aef7c65e61be394bacadaec200eb5b97f91c`. The 620 input tokens are handwritten
test data, not a subset of the upstream dictionary corpus. See `NOTICE.md`.

- `synthetic.data`: 315 keys, 620 tokens, 6,704 bytes.
- `synthetic.jsonl`: 1,268 complete C++ lookup responses, covering both exact
  and common-prefix lookup for all synthetic readings, extended readings,
  empty and absent queries. Order and duplicate surface forms are retained.
- `synthetic-input.jsonl`: all original 620 tokens before compression, emitted
  by `oracle fixture-inputs unused`. Rust must reproduce `synthetic.data` exactly
  with the fixture's small-cost threshold of 1 (the upstream default is 6).
- `loader.tsv`, `loader-id.def`, `loader-special-pos.def`, `loader-corrections.tsv`:
  handwritten loader edge cases and all 258 upstream voiced-sound table rules.
- `loader-input.jsonl`: 281 uncompressed tokens emitted by C++ TextDictionaryLoader,
  including three corrections. Covers tie order, duplicate corrections, missing
  values, existing readings, special POS labels and all normalization rules.
- `loader.data`: 2,500 bytes generated by C++ from that loaded input, using the
  default small-cost threshold. Rust reproduces these bytes from TSV.

Run `python3 tools/validate.py --bazelisk /path/to/bazelisk` to regenerate into
`validation-output/` and compare the generated files byte for byte with these fixtures.
Expected values must come from the C++ oracle, never from the Rust reader.
